answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a crystal as the anchor of the cost. A canyon stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a beacon...
